title: Background tracking + trace infrastructure (tracker, cross-process sidecar, forwarding trace sink, tree events)

findings.title: Grouped orphan report is packed into SubAgentCompletionEvent.summary with success=false, and announce_one renders `error` instead of `summary` on failure - every recovered partial result is discarded on the primary restart path
mark_consumed's running branch never calls record_announced, so a cancelled+consumed child stays `Settled && !announced` on disk and the next boot re-announces it as 'FINISHED ... do not repeat it'
summarize_orphans partitions on phase==Settled, so failed / timed_out / cancelled runs land in the 'FINISHED ... this work is done, do not repeat it' bucket
One-shot `announced` stamp and Abandoned tombstone are written before the notification is delivered; every announce_one bail-out path silently withdraws the notice with no retry on any later boot

Grouped orphan summary is unbounded: every recovered run's full 8 KiB partial_result is concatenated into one parent-turn prompt with no row cap, while the sibling `list` face caps rows and previews at 200 chars

Blocking fs I/O incl. fsync on tokio worker threads: one open+append per progress event from ForwardingTraceSink::on_trace, one write_atomic fsync per mark_consumed inside wait_any; twin process_journal batches via a flusher and rewrites in place for exactly this reason

list_for_scope reads and fully re-renders every retained record's trail (7-day retention) on every `subagent list`, discarding all but a 200-char preview; the append-only trail file itself has no size cap
record_settled appends to the trail before the index check, creating <slug>/result.txt directories with no state.json that read_all skips and the retention sweep can never prune

TOCTOU: a mark_consumed landing between mark_completed's running snapshot and its completed insert writes consume_on_completion onto an entry about to be removed, so the completed entry is born un-consumed (spurious announce on a cancel race)
MAX_COMPLETED_RESULTS eviction is process-global and cross-session: one busy session evicts another session's still-unread completed results, which then read as 'unknown request_id'
wait_any and unknown_ids clone the full CompletedSnapshot (entire final text + progress tail) per id per lap just to test presence; every process-wide completion wakes every waiter into another lap

Stale invariant comment: 'no code path ever holds two of this struct's locks at the same time' is contradicted by subagent_snapshot, which holds both read guards; the only record of the lock order states a rule the code does not follow
render_tool_result_preview serializes the entire tool output to a String (and re-scans it for a char count) to keep 200 chars, on every ToolCallCompleted of every background sub-agent

angles_checked_clean.verdict: Clean - OnceLock::get_or_init, Arc clone per caller. No process-exit cleanup needed (pure process memory); the durability gap it used to leave is what background_persistence closes.

angles_checked_clean.angle: running -> completed transition ordering (spurious NotFound window)
angles_checked_clean.verdict: Clean - completed is inserted (:552) before running is removed (:590), so an id is never absent from both maps; flat_nodes de-dupes by completed_ids (:1222-1263) and addressable prefers the running copy (:695-701).

Clean - Notified is created and enable()d before every state read (:921-923), the deadline arm is a select! against the notifier, and each lap builds a fresh Notified. AllDelivered terminates the drain loop; wait() maps it back to the single-agent answer.

angles_checked_clean.angle: wait_any scope re-check while parked (foreign completion claim)
angles_checked_clean.verdict: Clean - result_snapshot/running_meta go through addressable inside the loop (:936, :944), covered by wait_any_does_not_claim_a_foreign_completion_while_parked.

angles_checked_clean.angle: Result TTL / count cap (recent MAX_COMPLETED_RESULTS fix)
angles_checked_clean.verdict: Verified - register_with_meta -> insert_running -> cleanup(BACKGROUND_RESULT_TTL) at :475 (running guard dropped first), and mark_completed caps by count under the same write lock at :575-585. Both bounds hold regardless of spawn cadence. Only defect is the cross-session eviction (B2-10).
Clean - every acquisition in all four files uses unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) with a warn!, including the sidecar's STORE_DIR / INDEX mutexes.

No inversion today - every site releases `completed` before touching `running`; subagent_snapshot is the only two-lock holder and takes running->completed. Documented invariant is wrong though (B2-12).

Clean - registers presence-only, delists on Drop incl. panic unwind and future-drop, wakes waiters via notify_waiters; hidden from list_running/flat_nodes but visible to session_has_running / running_children_of / running_runs_of_session / cancel.

Clean - cancel_in_scope gates on addressable, fires the stored token; tree token + child_token wiring verified by tree_cancel_fires_tree_token_and_members_stay_enumerable; CancelGuard in spawn.rs terminates the bridge watcher on every exit path incl. panic.

Clean - registration + record_start happen before the permit is acquired (subagent_spawner/mod.rs:208), which is what makes a queued-then-cancelled child recoverable; the semaphore is session-keyed with Weak so it outlives the per-request SubagentTool.

Consistent - background spawns always attach at parent_id=None under the session root (spawn.rs:100), matching flat_nodes / running_children_of docs; lifecycle_from_outcome is the single source shared by the stored lifecycle and the live Settled event, with byte-exact cancel classification.

Clean - background_persistence::addressable is strict equality (the empty-root_session fail-open is fixed, :561-563) and list_for_scope uses the same predicate as lookup. Production SubagentTool always sets parent_session_id (run_loop/inner.rs:1054), so scope is never accidentally None.
Clean - slug() maps every non-[A-Za-z0-9_-] char to '_' and never yields empty; the 128-char truncation is a theoretical collision surface only, and every production id is a fresh UUID.

angles_checked_clean.angle: Redaction of the new disk egress
angles_checked_clean.verdict: Clean - task text and every trail line go through SecretMasker via mask_line before hitting disk; asserted on raw bytes by the_activity_trail_is_redacted_before_it_reaches_the_disk. record_settled's `outcome` field is a fixed label, not model text.

angles_checked_clean.angle: read_trail tail slice (UTF-8 / the take_while(..).last() fix)
angles_checked_clean.verdict: Correct - indices come from char_indices so the slice is on a boundary, and last() yields the smallest satisfying index (the real tail), not the first match. Cost of the full read is B2-07.

Correct - Running -> Abandoned tombstone is written to disk before returning, so a second boot does not re-report; start/mod.rs registers the announce subscriber before init_and_announce_orphans. The remaining defect is that the stamp precedes delivery (B2-04).

angles_checked_clean.angle: forwarding_trace_sink Arc aliasing / drop semantics / reentrancy
angles_checked_clean.verdict: Clean - no locks held across the inner sink call, tracker guard released inside push_progress before the persistence write and the tree emit; a post-completion event returns None and correctly suppresses the Progress emit; flush always forwards.

Clean - now_ms saturates instead of panicking, emit_tree_event short-circuits on an empty session id before tokio::spawn, and every caller is inside a runtime. flush() (the plausible non-runtime caller) does not emit.

None found - all unwrap/expect are #[cfg(test)]; integer conversions use try_from(..).unwrap_or(u64::MAX); string truncation is char-indexed in both preview_from_outcome and read_trail. Only theoretical site is Instant::now()+timeout in wait_any:916, and callers clamp the timeout.
